title: Telemetry harvest for kernel-level NVTX spans and per-kernel metrics
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Objective: Instrument the serving runtime to emit low-overhead, high-fidelity telemetry for per-kernel execution and NVTX ranges so engineers can correlate kernel selection and attention optimizations with tail latency, token-per-second throughput, and decodetime breakdowns.

Scope:
- Add NVTX range markers for prefill and decode phases, and for major runtime subsystems (tokenization, embedding lookup, KV cache reads/writes, attention kernel, FFN kernel, softmax/normalization kernels).
- Emit trace spans (OpenTelemetry-compatible) for prefill->decode transition and for kernel-level calls; include structured attributes: model_name, model_version, kernel_name, kernel_variant (e.g., cuBLAS, fused-attn, quant-kernel), device_id, seq_len, batch_size, shard_id, request_id.
- Capture per-kernel metrics: execution_time_ms, launch_overhead_ms, bytes_read, bytes_written, flops_estimate, occupancy_estimate.
- Provide both sampled traces for end-to-end root-span analysis and aggregated metrics (Prometheus histograms/counters and high-cardinality event logs) for dashboarding and alerting.

Design decisions:
- NVTX ranges should be placed at boundary of CUDA kernel launches and at high-level runtime state transitions; use a stable naming convention: rw:phase:{prefill|decode}:{component}:{kernel_variant}. Example: "rw:decode:attention:fused_attn_v2".
- Traces will be emitted via an OTel bridge; runtime will prefer an in-process micro-batcher to reduce overhead and flush on safe points (epoch end, request completion) with backpressure.
- Per-kernel timings use GPU timers where available (CUPTI or CUDA events) with a software fallback (host-side timestamping) for CPU-only flows.
- Sampling strategy: default 1% trace sampling across production, 100% for canary traffic or explicitly tagged requests; aggregated metrics emitted at all times.
- Cardinality: avoid unbounded label cardinality. Model version and kernel variant are OK; request_id should be a span attribute, not a metric label.

Implementation plan:
1) Library: implement small wrapper library (librw_telemetry) that exposes macros and C++ RAII scope helpers. Support Python/Go bindings in a follow-up.
2) Kernel registry: add registration hooks at kernel compile/selection time to record kernel metadata (name, tile sizes, quantization mode).
3) NVTX and span placement: instrument runtime scheduler at key points: scheduling decision, kernel submission, stream sync, and post-kernel processing.
4) Metrics export: expose Prometheus metrics endpoint for aggregated per-kernel counters; push detailed events to a scalable event store for offline analysis.
5) Dashboards and alerts: add pre-built Grafana dashboards and SLI rules (e.g., sudden spike in attention kernel latency by variant).

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Feature guarded behind a config flag (telemetry.enable_kernel_spans). Default on for staging and off for general production until canary evaluation.
- Gradual rollout: enable for dedicated and internal clusters first, then hosted canary customers.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for the telemetry wrapper and registry.
- Microbench harness that runs synthetic workload across a matrix of seq_len and batch_size to validate timing accuracy vs. baseline.
- End-to-end integration: validate trace->metric correlation by generating known delays in attention path and asserting downstream dashboards pick up signal.

Success criteria:
- Observability: Able to attribute 95% of tail ablatable latency (>=99th percentile) to a specific kernel variant or scheduling decision in the trace sampling set.
- Overhead: telemetry enabled should add <= 3% latency and <5% CPU overhead on production workloads at sampling 1%.
- Actionability: dashboards and alerts detect regression from a baseline perf run and provide an actionable root cause within 15 minutes.

Rollout tasks (high level):
- Code: librw_telemetry + kernel registration + NVTX spans (ENG-9247).
- Backend: OTel collector configuration + Prometheus metrics + ingestion pipeline changes (ENG-9184).
- Dashboards: add Grafana panels and example runbooks (PM/Observability).

Notes: Keep kernel instrumentation logic isolated so model compilation paths (AOT/ONNX/fused kernels) can opt-in. Ensure telemetry config supports redaction of sensitive attributes and respects customer PII settings in Private deployments.

traces_tag_convention: rw.phase / rw.component / kernel_variant -> used as span attributes; request_id only on spans not metrics
implementation_notes: Start with C++ wrapper, expose minimal Python helper for dev debugging. Use RAII scopes: RW_SCOPE_NVTX(name, attrs...). Avoid dynamic string concat in hot paths by pre-registering common span names at startup.
